theater: 江東太湖流域吳興、吳郡、會稽

battle.name: 沈法興起事
battle.theater: 江東太湖流域吳興、吳郡、會稽
battle.brief: 大業十三年冬隋煬帝死於江都，越王楊侑在越州即位，吳興豪族沈法興乘亂起兵，取吳興、吳郡、會稽、餘杭四郡，一度擁兵二萬，與越王侑及唐廷周旋，至武德二年（619）為部將所殺。卡面羅馬短劍靠橫木護手護住握柄，江東隋軍卻用沒有護手的環首刀，硬以鐔角與重心換取抽刀即刺的節奏。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 沈法興起事爆發在隋朝崩解的江東，起義方是一支以吳興鄉豪為核心的地方武裝，官方一方則是各據城自守的隋朝州縣與坐鎮越州的中樞。起義集團的核心是吳興、吳郡一帶的豪族與渠帥：沈法興靠家世、鄉誼與私人部曲起家，李子川、孫紹等吳郡豪族各領部眾加盟，外圍則是逃戶、逃兵、被徵發未還的役夫，以及郡兵與鄉兵。史稱他一度擁兵二萬，但這支部隊沒有常備建制，糧餉、編制、指揮全靠臨時推舉，渠帥各領一軍，事權極易分裂。控制區由吳興郡城起步，先取吳郡，再及會稽、餘杭，把太湖下游的郡縣與漕運線握在手中。官方的隋朝江南東道各州縣並非一體：吳郡太守、吳興太守等各守城邑，靠郡兵、縣兵與徵來的鄉兵固守城牆與水門，援軍指望越州方向或從江北南下；越王楊侑在越州即位後成為名義上的中心，卻只能靠一紙詔書和零星部隊維持秩序。同一時期，淮南有杜伏威、嶺南有馮盎各自割據，江北則是王世充與李淵相持；沈法興的位置，正在這張互不照應的權力網絡中間。日後唐朝以招撫收編的方式接管這片地方，衝突的性質由叛隋轉為叛唐，再回到受唐招撫。
countriesEn: Shen Faxing's rising broke out in Jiangdong at the moment the Sui order was coming apart. The rebel side was a local armed force built around the village elite of Wuxing, while the official side consisted of the Sui prefectures and counties each holding its own city, together with the court that sat at Yue Prefecture. At the core of the rebel group stood the great families and local militia leaders of the Wuxing and Wujun region: Shen Faxing rose on the strength of his pedigree, his ties with the countryside and his private retainers, while men such as Li Zichuan and Sun Shao of Wujun brought their own bands in with them; around them were runaway households, deserters, levies conscripted and never sent home, and the commandery and village troops of the district. The histories say he once numbered twenty thousand men, but this force had no standing establishment: pay, organisation and command all rested on ad hoc appointments, each militia leader commanding his own contingent, and authority could split at any moment. The area under his control began at the commandery seat of Wuxing, then took Wujun and reached Kuaiji and Yuhang, giving him the commanderies of the lower Taihu lake together with the canal grain route. The Sui administration of the Jiangnan East Circuit was not a single body: the prefect of Wujun, the commandant of Wuxing and the rest each held a city, relying on commandery troops, county troops and conscripted villagers to man the walls and the water gates, while relief could only be expected from the direction of Yue Prefecture or from the north across the river. After Prince Yue Yang You was enthroned at Yue he became the nominal centre of authority, yet he could hold the region together only by edict and by the occasional detachment. At the same time Du Fuwei held the south of the Huai, Feng Ang held Lingnan, and to the north Wang Shichong and Li Yuan were locked in a stalemate; Shen Faxing stood in the middle of this web of powers that supported no one. Later the Tang took the region over by amnesty and absorption, and the character of the conflict shifted from rebellion against the Sui to rebellion against the Tang and then back to submission to Tang grace.
people: 沈法興是這場起事唯一留下完整姓名的首領，吳興人，出身江南望族，父沈君雄仕隋，曾任吳郡太守，家族在吳興一郡之內有數代經營的田產、僮客與鄉里影響力。史稱他少時驕侈好田獵；大業末年天下大亂，他與吳郡豪族李子川、孫紹等聚兵於吳興郡城，據城自守，隨後以討逆為名號令江東。吳郡人羅子拿在蘇州起兵反，殺害隋朝吳郡太守，越王楊侑派李子川討之不利，沈法興乘勢與李子川部合擊，攻下吳郡；這一戰的指揮者，史料或記其族弟，或記其部將，或略而不書，說法不一。越王楊侑聞訊遣使入湖州，授沈法興吳郡王（一說吳王），此後他以受封之名徵發、置吏、出兵，與楊侑的名分既互相利用又互相防備。隋室宗室之中，楊侑在越州、楊侗在洛陽，兩人各自求援，江南的沈法興並未真正歸附任何一邊。唐高祖李淵建唐之後，江南局勢重估，沈法興先遣使入朝通款，得授吳郡王與湖州刺史一類的羈縻名位，隨後稱疾不朝、逗留境內，與部眾的裂痕終於致命：武德二年（619），其帳下人馬合謀將他殺死，眾隨之潰散。與他同時起兵的豪族李子川、孫紹，以及在吳郡起兵的羅子拿，姓名雖存，事蹟都只剩斷簡殘篇，兵數、佈置與勝負細節都無從核實。
peopleEn: Shen Faxing is the only leader of this rising whose name survives in full in the standard records. A native of Wuxing in Jiangnan, he came from an established local family; his father Shen Junxiong served the Sui and was once prefect of Wujun, and the clan had several generations of accumulated land, household retainers and local influence within the single commandery of Wuxing. The histories describe him as extravagant and fond of hunting when young. As the Sui order collapsed at the end of the Daye era he mustered troops with the Wujun elite such as Li Zichuan and Sun Shao, held the seat of Wuxing commandery, and then used the language of punishing the rebels to order Jiangdong on his own account. Luo Zina, a man of Wujun, rose in revolt at Suzhou and killed the Sui prefect of Wujun; Prince Yue Yang You sent Li Zichuan against him without success, and Shen Faxing took the opportunity to strike together with Li Zichuan's men and take Wujun. Who commanded that column is not agreed in the sources: some name a kinsman of Shen, others a subordinate, and some records simply pass it over. When Yang You heard of the rising he sent an envoy to Huzhou and ennobled Shen Faxing as Prince of Wujun (in one account as Prince of Wu); thereafter Shen used the dignity of that title to levy men, appoint officials and send out troops, and his position vis-a-vis Yang You was at once a mutual convenience and a mutual guard. Among the Sui imperial clan, Yang You was at Yue and Yang Tong at Luoyang, each seeking support on his own account, and Shen Faxing in Jiangdong did not genuinely attach himself to either of them. After Li Yuan founded the Tang the balance in Jiangdong was reweighed: Shen Faxing first sent an envoy to court and got in touch, receiving a nominal appointment of the kind that bound a distant governor, such as Prince of Wujun and commandant of Huzhou; he then claimed illness and did not come to court, staying inside his own territory, and here his rupture with his own followers turned fatal. In the second year of Wude (619) men of his own camp combined to kill him, and his bands scattered. The names of the great families who rose with him, Li Zichuan and Sun Shao, and of Luo Zina who rose in Wujun, do survive, but their doings survive only in broken fragments; their numbers, dispositions and the details of their victories cannot be verified.
kits: 卡面這件古羅馬短劍並沒有出現在江南的戰場上，它在這場戰役裡的位置，是作為刺擊型短兵器的祖型與對照。gladius 大約在公元前三世紀定型：劍身雙刃、主刃平直，重心集中在前段，柄上橫木與握纏供單手穩定握持，羅馬步兵把它與大型圓盾配合使用，盾擋住來勢，劍從盾的掩護邊緣之外刺出，短兵相接靠的是刺突的節奏而不是揮砍的力道。隋末唐初的江東，實際握在軍人手上的是形制相近的另一套東西：環首刀，直刃無弧，刀身狹長，鐔作環形以便懸掛佩帶，握在手中同樣以刺為先鋒、斬為補充；另有儀刀、佩劍與身體更長的直刃刀，屬於同一條東亞刀劍譜系的早期形態。環首刀與 gladius 並非同一件器物，在戰術功能上卻高度同構：都要求單手握持，能在窄地與混戰裡迅速刺出，並與盾牌、長矛配合，構成步戰的三件套。起義軍的近身兵器則大量來自民間就地取材：削尖的竹木、舊銅器改成的矛頭、柴刀與農具改造的短刀，另有以皮革、木板、藤條製成的步盾與小型圓盾。遠射方面，江南水網密布而林木充足，弓弩使用密度高，弩以蹶張弩與腰弓弩為主，箭以竹木為杆、翎羽為羽；兵甲以皮甲、網甲為多，兜鍪多為皮製或銅片拼接，鎧甲大量依賴民間自備。攻城具則沿用舊隋留下的撞車、雲梯、火箭與壕塞木柵，但起義方多以封鎖水門、斷糧、策反守將來解決城池，而不是靠大型器械硬攻。真正值得一比的還有格擋：gladius 的橫木護手專門攔住對方的刃口順著自己的劍身滑到手背，環首刀卻沒有護手，隋唐步卒遇上這種局面，要嘛加大刃角、把刀反握以鐔朝前當錐使，要嘛放棄格擋退開一步重來。水鄉的接戰環境把這個差距放大了：舟板、跳板、水門閘口窄到退不了，一旦持刀的手被對方帶偏，整個人就落水。所以 618 年江東最實用的近身兵器，仍是重心靠後、可以單手抽出即刺的環首刀；羅馬短劍在這裡標示的不是刺突節奏，而是一種用護手把格擋失敗擋在門外的相反解法。
kitsEn: The Roman gladius on the card never appeared in Jiangdong; what the card does show is a guarding problem answered in two opposite ways, and the second of them is the one that actually worked in 618. The gladius took its final form around the third century BCE: a double-edged blade with a straight main edge, its weight concentrated toward the front, with a cross-piece and wrapped grip on the hilt for a stable one-handed hold. Roman infantry used it together with the large round shield, the shield turning the incoming blow while the sword was thrust from beyond the covered edge of the shield; in close fighting what decided the matter was the rhythm of the thrust, not the swing of a cutting stroke. In Jiangdong at the end of the Sui and the beginning of the Tang, what soldiers actually held was a closely related set of implements from another tradition: the ring-pommel dao, with a straight edge and no curve, a narrow blade and a ring-shaped pommel for hanging at the belt, gripped so that the thrust again came first and the cut was the supplement; there were also the ceremonial dao, side swords and longer straight-edged blades, early forms of the same East Asian family of dao and jian. The ring-pommel dao is not the same object as a gladius, but the two are close in tactical function: each is meant for a one-handed grip, each can be thrust out quickly in a narrow place or a confused melee, and each works together with shield and spear as the triad of infantry combat. The rebels' close-combat weapons were largely taken from local materials: sharpened bamboo and wood, spearheads reworked from old bronze vessels, short blades beaten out of kitchen and farm tools, together with step shields and small round shields made of leather, planking or rattan. At range, the dense waterways and abundant woodland of Jiangnan made bows and crossbows common, the crossbows being mostly the strongman type and the small waist-bow type, with arrows of bamboo or wood shafts and feather fletching. Armour was largely hide and mail, with helmets most often of leather or riveted bronze plate, so that the equipment of the common soldiers depended heavily on what households could supply. For sieges the rebel side used the battering rams, scaling ladders, fire arrows and wooden palisades left over from the Sui, yet it usually took a city by sealing the water gates, cutting the grain road and turning the garrison, rather than by grinding at it with heavy equipment. One further comparison is worth making, and it concerns parrying. The cross-piece of a gladius exists to stop an opponent's edge from sliding down the blade and onto the wielder's hand; the ring-pommel dao has no guard at all, and when a Sui or Tang foot soldier met that situation he either widened the edge and reversed the grip so that the pommel ring led as a point, or gave up the parry and stepped back to try again. The fighting ground of the water country magnified that difference: the deck of a boat, a boarding plank or the gate of a water gate was too narrow to give ground, and if the knife hand was turned aside by the opponent's blow the whole man went into the water. The practical close-combat weapon in the Jiangdong of 618 was therefore still the ring-pommel dao, whose weight sat close to the hand and which could be drawn and thrust in a single motion. What the Roman short sword marks here is not the rhythm of the thrust but the opposite solution, one that keeps a failed parry outside the door by means of a guard.
tactics: 這場起事沒有留下可考的戰役圖，但從地理、器械與事件序列可以重建它的打法。第一步是憑鄉誼迅速成軍：豪族拿出私兵與僮客，渠帥帶領鄉兵，逃戶逃兵填充人數，郡縣的舊吏與文書隨之而來，使新起的武裝很快具備徵發、分派糧賦與維持秩序的能力。第二步是取城而非野戰：吳興郡城是起義的支撐點，取得它就等於取得太湖西岸的倉、鹽與丁口；此後沈法興不急於與隋朝官軍在開闊地決戰，而是以舟船與小艇沿吳松江、江南運河與太湖航道推進，穩住會稽與餘杭的外圍。第三步是合擊：吳郡之圍牽涉羅子拿部與越王楊侑所遣李子川部，雙方各懷打算，沈法興選擇與其中一方聯合，而不是同時對抗三方，用封鎖水門、斷糧道與策反城內守將的方式瓦解守軍，避開正面攻城造成的消耗。第四步是轉向防守與自保：控制四郡之後，他沒有北上或西進的打算，重心轉為保境、收租、徵兵與對唐周旋，這一階段的部署以控扼要道、囤兵於吳郡與吳興、遣使往來為主。整體而言，這是一場典型的水鄉地方割據：靠舟船解決距離，靠城垣解決風險，靠徵發解決兵源，最終卻因部眾龐雜、各渠帥各懷心思而無法整合。環首刀與短劍式的刺突在其中只是巷戰與接觸戰的最後一步，並非決定性環節。
tacticsEn: No map of the fighting survives from this rising, but the way it was fought can be reconstructed from the geography, the equipment and the sequence of events. The first step was to raise an army quickly on the strength of local acquaintance: the great families put up their private retainers and household servants, the militia leaders brought in village bands, runaways and deserters filled the ranks, and former commandery clerks and scribes came with them, so that the new armed force was soon able to levy, allot grain dues and keep order. The second step was to take towns rather than to fight a battle in the open. The commandery seat of Wuxing was the hinge of the rising; holding it meant holding the granaries, the salt and the registered households of the west shore of the lake. After that Shen Faxing was in no hurry to meet the Sui field forces on open ground; he pushed by boat and small skiff along the Wusong river, the Jiangnan canal and the channels of the lake, and stabilised the outer positions at Kuaiji and Yuhang. The third step was a combined attack. The siege of Wujun involved the men of Luo Zina and the detachment sent by Prince Yue Yang You under Li Zichuan, each party with its own design, and Shen Faxing chose to act with one of them rather than to oppose all three at once; he broke the garrison by sealing the water gates, cutting the supply road and turning officers inside the city, avoiding the wastage of a frontal assault. The fourth step was a turn towards defence and self-preservation. Once the four commanderies were in his hands he had no intention of marching north or west; his weight shifted to holding his ground, collecting rents, levying men and managing relations with the Tang court, and the deployments of this phase consisted of holding the key roads, massing troops at Wujun and Wuxing, and exchanging envoys. In the whole, this was a typical local rising in a watery region: distance was solved by boats, risk by city walls, manpower by levying, and in the end it fell apart because the host was too large and too mixed and each militia leader had his own interests. The thrust of the ring-pommel dao, and of the short-sword manner of fighting, played only the last step in street fighting and in contact, and was never the decisive element.
data: 可用的數字並不多，但幾個尺度大致可以確定。隋朝在大業初年的登記戶口接近八百九十萬，口數超過四千六百萬；吳郡、會稽、吳興是全國人口最稠密、賦稅最重的郡份之一。為供三征高麗前後的大軍與東巡江都的漕運，江南長期承擔轉輸與徵發，役夫與民戶的耗損是全國性的。時間點上，大業十三年（617）十一月宇文化及在江都弒隋煬帝，隋室名存實亡；越王楊侑在越州即位，改元太平；武德元年（618）沈法興在吳興起事；武德二年（619），王世充在洛陽篡越王侑自立，同年沈法興死於部眾之手。兵員方面，通行史籍說沈法興擁兵二萬，《舊唐書》與《資治通鑑》在這一數字上大體相符；對照吳興、吳郡、會稽三郡動輒數十萬的戶口，這支部隊本質上是地方性武裝，而不是能與北方任何一支大軍抗衡的兵力。地理尺度上，太湖水面約二千三百平方公里，吳興郡城（今湖州）至吳郡城（今蘇州）沿水陸約一百五十至二百公里；自起事到覆亡，前後不足兩年。
dataEn: Few usable figures survive, but several scales can be fixed with reasonable confidence. In the early years of the Daye era the registered households of the Sui numbered close to 8.9 million and the population exceeded 46 million; Wujun, Kuaiji and Wuxing were among the most densely populated and most heavily taxed commanderies of the empire. To feed the armies of the three campaigns against Goguryeo and the grain traffic of the emperor's eastern tours to Jiangdu, Jiangdong bore a long share of transport and conscription, and the drain on corvée labourers and on peasant households was empire-wide. As to the sequence: in the eleventh month of Daye 13 (617) Yuwen Huaji killed the Sui emperor at Jiangdu and the dynasty was a name only; Prince Yue Yang You was enthroned at Yue under the era title Taiping; in Wude 1 (618) Shen Faxing rose at Wuxing; in Wude 2 (619) Wang Shichong usurped Yang You at Luoyang and in the same year Shen Faxing was killed by his own men. On numbers: the standard histories say Shen Faxing had twenty thousand men, and the Jiu Tang Shu and the Zi Zhi Tong Jian agree closely on that figure; set against the tens of thousands of households in the three commanderies of Wuxing, Wujun and Kuaiji, this was in truth a local force and not an army capable of standing against any of the great northern ones. On geography: the surface of Taihu lake is about 2,300 square kilometres, and the commandery seat of Wuxing (present Huzhou) lies some 150 to 200 kilometres from the seat of Wujun (present Suzhou) by water and road; from the rising to the collapse of the force, less than two years passed.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層。第一層是隋朝自己製造的：煬帝頻頻東巡江都、營造宮室，三征高麗把全國丁口推上前線，江北、江南的漕運與徭役攤派年年加劇，江都一帶在大業七年（611）前後已爆發過民變，民間對郡兵與徵發的怨懼與恐懼同時上升。當大業十三年十一月宇文化及在江都弒帝、越王楊侑在越州即位，隋朝的中央權威實際上只剩下幾座城和一批各自打算的官，這是所有起事共享的時機。第二層是江南本身的結構：吳興、吳郡、會稽一帶田租、鹽利、絲織與造船都極發達，而這些資源長期由郡縣官府與地方豪族分割，一旦朝廷失控，最先伸手的自然是能調動鄉里、又能號召水陸人手的本地人物。沈法興正是這樣的人：他有家世、有鄉誼、有私兵，又熟諳吳興一郡的戶籍與倉場，能把起兵辦成一場有秩序的徵發。第三層是名分的需要：越王楊侑需要一個能在江東替朝廷守土、替自己爭取江南的強者，雙方因此互相利用；沈法興需要一個奉詔討逆的名號，好把自己從地方叛亂變成替隋室平亂的義師。於是起事本身同時具備了反隋與擁隋的雙重面貌。
causeEn: There are three layers to the reasons the fighting began. The first was manufactured by the Sui itself: the Jian emperor toured Jiangdu again and again and built palaces, and the three campaigns against Goguryeo threw the whole register of the empire onto the front; in the north and in Jiangdong the grain traffic and the levy of corvée grew heavier every year, and around the year 611 a rising of the common people had already broken out in the region of Jiangdu, so that resentment and fear of the district troops and of the levies rose together. When in the eleventh month of Daye 13 Yuwen Huaji killed the emperor at Jiangdu and Yang You was enthroned at Yue, the central authority of the Sui had in fact shrunk to a few cities and a set of officials each with his own plan, and that was the moment shared by every rising of the time. The second layer lay in the structure of Jiangdong itself: in the districts of Wuxing, Wujun and Kuaiji the rents, the salt, the silk and the shipbuilding were all highly developed, and these resources had long been divided between the commandery offices and the local great families. The moment the court lost control, the first to reach out were those who could mobilise a countryside and call out men for the water and the roads, and Shen Faxing was exactly such a man: pedigree, village connections, a private following, and a working knowledge of the household registers and granaries of Wuxing that let him turn an insurrection into an orderly levy. The third layer was the need for legitimacy. Yang You needed a strongman in Jiangdong who would hold the land for the court and win the region for himself, so the two used each other; Shen Faxing needed the title of one who obeyed the edict and punished the rebels, so that he would be a loyalist enforcing order on behalf of the Sui rather than a local rebel. The rising therefore wore two faces at once: it was against the Sui and for the Sui.
impact: 這場起事在時間上很短，但它決定的東西不少。第一，它把江南的割據代價壓到最低。吳郡、會稽一帶若在刀兵中反覆爭奪，受損的會是唐初最需要的漕源、絲織與造船；而沈法興兩年就倒向唐廷，江南的州縣衙署、倉場、里甲與手工業在相對安寧的環境下被接管，隋末江南的生齒與戶籍沒有經歷一次大規模的消耗。第二，它讓唐室的統一從北方推進變成南北合流。武德年間唐廷先後平定蕭銑、馮盎、杜伏威、梁師都與王世充等割據，江南是最後一塊拼圖，而沈法興早早覆亡，使這塊拼圖幾乎沒有經過戰火。第三，它留下了一種地方權力的樣板：沈法興的部曲、渠帥與鄉里關係網，在戰亂結束後被唐廷改編為州縣鄉里的基幹，吳興沈氏一門後來仍多出任地方官員與將領，豪族與中央的關係由對抗回到合作。第四，它也留下一個教訓：以擁立宗室而非自立取得名分的割據者，合法性完全寄生於宗室，一旦宗室被各自的盟友消滅，便失去了可以退守的位置。
impactEn: The rising was short in time, but a good deal followed from it. First, it kept the cost of the Jiangdong break-up at its lowest. Had Wujun and Kuaiji been fought over repeatedly with weapons, the losers would have been exactly the grain supply, the silk and the shipbuilding that the early Tang most needed; and since Shen Faxing turned to the Tang within two years, the offices, granaries, local registers and crafts of Jiangdong were taken over amid relative quiet, and the people and households of the region escaped the mass consumption that a civil war would have inflicted. Second, it turned the Tang unification from a northern advance into a convergence from north and south. Through the Wude years the court put down Xiao Xian, Feng Ang, Du Fuwei, Liang Shidu and Wang Shichong in turn; Jiangdong was the last piece of the puzzle, and the early collapse of Shen Faxing meant that piece was barely touched by war. Third, it left a model of local power: the bands, militia leaders and networks of village ties that Shen Faxing commanded were, after the fighting, folded by the Tang into the backbone of the prefectures and villages, and the Shen clan of Wuxing later produced many local officials and officers, so that the relation between the great families and the centre changed from confrontation back to cooperation. Fourth, it left a lesson: a pretender whose legitimacy rests on supporting an imperial prince rather than on establishing himself has nowhere to retreat once that prince is destroyed by his own allies.
result: 結果分兩步。先是起義成功：沈法興在吳興聚兵，隨後取得吳郡，會稽、餘杭亦歸其勢力，一度以受封吳郡王（說法不一，一作吳王）之名號令江東，擁兵約二萬，據地跨太湖兩岸，是隋末江南聲勢最大的地方割據者。接著是迅速崩解：武德二年（619），他遣使向唐朝通款，接受吳郡王與湖州刺史一類的羈縻官職，兵眾解散、府庫散盡，此後又稱疾不朝、逗留境內不肯入覲，與部眾及朝廷互相猜忌；同年，其帳下將士發難，沈法興被自己人殺死，所部隨之散入州縣，吳郡、吳興、會稽重新回到隋朝舊有的州縣框架，隨即由唐廷接管。從大業十三年冬起事到武德二年身死，不足兩年，兵不血刃而州郡歸唐。對歷史而言，這場起事既證明隋末江南存在足以割據的武裝與社會基礎，也證明依靠擁立宗室與虛名封爵的割據無法長久：隋朝覆亡之後，江南的秩序最終不是靠打仗重建，而是靠改換旗幟與換一套官吏體系重建。
resultEn: The outcome came in two stages. First the rising succeeded: Shen Faxing mustered men at Wuxing, then took Wujun, and Kuaiji and Yuhang came under his sway as well; for a time he ordered Jiangdong in the name of the princedom he had received as Prince of Wujun (accounts differ, in one as Prince of Wu), with about twenty thousand men and territory on both shores of Taihu lake, and he was the greatest local pretender in Jiangdong at the end of the Sui. Then came the rapid collapse. In the second year of Wude (619) he sent an envoy to the Tang court and made his submission, taking a nominal appointment of the kind that tied a distant governor, such as Prince of Wujun and commandant of Huzhou; his troops were dispersed and his stores emptied, and he then claimed illness and did not come to court, remaining in his own territory and mistrusting both the court and his own men. In that same year some of his officers rose against him and killed him; what remained of his forces scattered into the commanderies, and Wujun, Wuxing and Kuaiji returned to the framework of Sui commanderies and counties, soon after to be taken over by the Tang court. From the rising in the winter of Daye 13 to his death in Wude 2 less than two years passed, and the commanderies passed to the Tang without a battle being fought over them. For history the rising demonstrated both that the late Sui Jiangdong held the armed force and the social structure able to sustain a secession, and that a secession resting on supporting an imperial prince and on empty princely titles could not last: after the fall of the Sui the order of Jiangdong was rebuilt not by fighting but by changing the banners and replacing the administrative personnel.
